title: 🐛 fix(egressrelay): flush streamed bytes that cannot begin a secret (#4251)
body:
maskingBody held back the last longest-1 bytes of every upstream read, so
each streamed model event that ended a read reached the guest one
inter-event gap late, and the last one only at upstream EOF. The masker
now stops only where a value form could begin and run past the read, so
it holds back a proper prefix of a form and sends everything else at once.
No form is ever emitted split across reads.

The plain-http path to Config.Local destinations copied the body without
flushing, so the self-host relay batched events until the handler
returned. It now flushes after each masked read.

maskingBody also reuses one read buffer instead of allocating 32 KiB per
upstream read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: ✨ feat(build-cli): mount an overlay's .smithers onto a pinned upstream checkout (#4217)
body:
An overlay repository holds only .smithers/. Its .smithers/config.ts
default-exports S.Mounts({ <name>: S.Mount({ repository, ref, track, drift,
patches, overlay }) }). Every build-CLI command run from the overlay now
materializes the mount before it plans: it reads the tracked branch and
applies the drift policy (warn, refuse, follow), fetches the pinned commit
into .mounts/<name>, commits the declared patches on top, lays the overlay's
.smithers/ over the checkout, and opens the checkout as the workspace.
Upstream is only read; edits in the checkout, edits to a laid file, and
overlay files that collide with tracked upstream files are refused, never
discarded.

The hook is one call in openPackageIndex, so labels, caching, sandboxing,
and every rule work unchanged against the checkout. The design, the
rejected run-from-overlay alternative, and the patch and upstream-PR flow
are in packages/smithers/build/build-cli/docs/concepts/mounts.md.

title: 🐛 fix(stack): let a proposal wait while the stack rebases its own sealed capture
body:
J5 still failed TODO C now and then: when the earlier TODO's head moved
C's prefix, the stack had already taken C's sealed submission as a
pending capture to rebase, and stack.propose refused that as
reserved_prefix_mismatch. The proposal now also waits when the pending
capture holds the run's own sealed submission and its checks passed,
and once the stack consumes that capture onto the new prefix the stale
proposal is refused as reserved_candidate_rebased, as a native rebase
already was. A capture of other bytes, or of bytes never verified,
still refuses.

The prefix refusal now logs the facts it decided on (state, generations,
capture and rebase markers, heads), so the next race names itself.

Refs #4086

title: 🐛 fix(agent): re-drive a parked TODO run when a steer wakes it
body:
A review steer on a TODO in review never reached the run (J10: "Amend
updates the same PR" stayed working for 15 minutes). The TODO run parks
on an event wait for stack events after its proposal. Control.steer
claimed that parked run in the host process and journaled
control.steer.woke, but the executor's resume bridge followed only
control.run.resume and control.run.resumed, so the claimed row read
running while nothing drove the engine execution.

The bridge now takes up control.steer.woke as a delegated resume: the
engine records no wake for an event park, so a polling resume would
drive nothing, and a delegated one enters the body, which drains the
queued steer. It grants no released child a retry and still refuses a
quarantine park.

Refs #4086

title: 🐛 fix(stack): propose the rebased candidate when an earlier TODO moves the prefix
body:
J5 failed TODO C as a user fault: an earlier TODO's verified head became
C's prefix after C's candidate was accepted but before the stack proposed
it, and stack.propose refused with reserved_prefix_mismatch. Parallel
TODOs hit this whenever a predecessor verifies during a later TODO's
checks.

stack.propose for the run's own accepted candidate now waits (202) and
asks the stack for a pass while the prefix moves. Once the stack has
rebased that candidate to a new generation, the stale proposal is
refused as reserved_candidate_rebased, and the delivery captures the
rebased generation and proposes it (spec 10.4.1: clean rebase,
candidate, check, propose), up to three times. Any other refusal still
ends the run, and bytes still pending capture still refuse.

Refs #4086

title: 🐛 fix(flows): capture every TODO plan callback so a parked TODO resumes
body:
A TODO that asked a question failed the moment it resumed: "The rebuilt
plan differs from the recorded plan" (plan_changed, #3906). The durable
interpreter records the plan digest, and an inline callback has a
process-local identity that changes on every body build, so the rebuilt
todo plan never matched, even in the same process. J2, J3 and J4 all
stopped at Needs you.

Wrap every plan callback in the TODO flow and the coding step flows in
Node.capture, as LandVibe already does (d7455524e9). The TODO flow's
digest moves, so builtin_flows.json pins the new one, and the
coding-request wiki page excerpts request-flow.ts to stay inside the
30 kB review budget.

A typed catch's error-schema filter is still a process-local identity,
so a resume after a host restart still refuses; that is the plan
package's, tracked separately.

Refs #4086

title: 🚚 refactor(repo): move this repository's flows to .smithers/flows (M-49)
body:
The repository's own flows, automation modules and their package move from
a root flows/ to .smithers/flows/, the location the product discovers
(mvp.md M-49). `smthrs flow list` now lists them: 82 flows.

- Workspace members `.smithers/flows`, `.smithers/flows/coding` and
  `.smithers/flows/review/seeded-bugs`; labels become `//.smithers/flows:*`
  in PACKAGE.ts, ci.yml, the drift workflows, release.yml, release-gates,
  cloud.sh, the check inventory and every test that pins them. Relative
  imports in and into the moved tree gain the extra level.
- `pnpm docs:check` and `pnpm docs:sync` start the docs-sync flow, and the
  release job's changelog, build, API-baseline, restore and publish steps
  start their release flows (`smthrs flow start ... --wait`). Pack and smoke
  stay plain `node` so the Node-floor step proves the tarballs on that
  runtime. The release gate scanner treats a literal flow start as a flow
  step, not a target-graph gate, as it treated the `node` steps it replaced.
- The Cloud CI bootstrap moves to .github/scripts/ci/ beside the
  reference-host hooks: `.smithers/` keeps only what 1.0 owns there. Each
  CI command gets its own cloud gate again, and its contract suite reads
  the drift steps from trusted-drift.yml.
- The wiki flow admits `.smithers/flows/` sources, and docs-sync declares
  the irreversible tier discovery already assigned it.
- Retired-root fixtures (`flows/todo/flow.ts` as a stale root), persisted
  tags (`flows/memory/MemoryError`), workflow-definition paths and the
  shipped todo flow's bytes keep their old spelling, so recorded identities
  and digests do not move.
- The check inventory reader also tries `flows/evidence/check-commands.json`,

before its first letter, digit or `_`; `.`, `..` and option-like words stay
refused.

Refs #4092

title: 🐛 fix(agent): settle a void flow's completion as null so its run completes
body:
`agent/run` declares `success: Schema.Unknown`, which the JSON codec reads as
any JSON value. A flow whose success is `Schema.Void` completes with
`undefined`, so engine-store degraded the settlement into
`UnencodableResult` and `smthrs flow start --wait` reported the run failed
though its flow completed (the docs-sync and issue-claim flows).
`settlementSuccess` settles absence as `null` and every JSON value unchanged.

Refs #4092
